text: dsh-plugin-dew（DSH 插件，DSH 工具）：在 DSH 中查看 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 和 DSH 的本机会话状态，并查询部分 agent 的计划任务。它注册 agent_sessions 和 agent_scheduled_tasks 两个只读工具，从磁盘读取会话日志，将活动整理为待你处理、运行中、已完成或空闲；会话结果包含项目、摘要和时间，可按 agent、状态及回看时长筛选。计划任务工具列出日程与下次运行时间。适合同时使用多个编码 agent、需要掌握任务进度或查看已有自动任务的 DSH 用户。配置可选择扫描对象、默认回看时长，并可隐藏会话摘要。

dsh-plugin-dew adds two read-only DSH tools. agent_sessions summarizes local sessions from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and DSH, with state and time filters. agent_scheduled_tasks lists recurring jobs and next run times. It helps users check agent progress and schedules.
我想从 DSH 里看看 Claude Code、Codex 和其他编码 agent 现在跑到哪了。
Can I check which local coding sessions are running or waiting for me from DSH?
帮我列出本机配置的 Codex 自动任务和它们下一次的运行时间。
dsh-plugin-dew 的功能「会话状态」：调用 agent_sessions 汇总本地多个编码 agent 的会话，返回状态、项目和摘要，并支持筛选。
dsh-plugin-dew 的功能「计划任务」：调用 agent_scheduled_tasks 查看定时任务的名称、日程、下次运行时间和启用状态。
dsh-plugin-dew 使用前须知：会话摘要可能包含对话片段，并作为工具结果交给模型提供方；可将 redactSummaries 设为 true，仅返回状态和项目等信息。（见 lib/index.js:74-84,87-90）

dsh-plugin-dew README · dsh-plugin-dew：**See what your other coding agents are doing — from inside DSH.**

You run Claude Code in one window, Codex in another, maybe Cursor too. DSH can't
see any of it. This plugin gives DSH two read-only tools that parse the session
logs those agents already write to disk, and normalize everything to one
vocabulary: **needs you / running / done / idle**.

```
> is anything waiting on me?

3 matching sessions; 11 scanned over the last 8h (needs you 1, running 2, done 8, idle 0).

dsh-plugin-dew README · dsh-plugin-dew：It is a port of the readers behind [Dew](https://github.com/cinderzhan/dew), a
macOS status bar for the same data.

dsh-plugin-dew README · Install：Requires Node 20+. Reading DSH's own compressed transcripts additionally needs a
runtime with `zlib.zstdDecompressSync` (Node 23.8+); without it the other three
agents still work.

dsh-plugin-dew README · `agent_sessions`：Lists sessions and what each one is doing.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `agents` | string[] | Restrict to `claude_code`, `codex`, `cursor`, `dsh`. Omit for all. |
| `state` | string | One of the four states, or `active` (default, everything but idle), or `all`. |
| `within_hours` | integer | Lookback. Defaults to 8. |
| `limit` | integer | Cap on returned rows, highest priority first. Defaults to 25. |

dsh-plugin-dew README · `agent_sessions`：Good for: *"is my Claude Code run finished?"*, *"which agent is blocked on me?"*,
and — before you start editing — *"is another agent already working in this
directory?"*

dsh-plugin-dew README · `agent_scheduled_tasks`：Lists recurring agent jobs and when each fires next: Codex automations (RRULE)
and Claude Code scheduled tasks (cron), evaluated locally.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `agents` | string[] | Restrict to specific agents. |
| `include_disabled` | boolean | Include switched-off tasks. Defaults to false. |

dsh-plugin-dew README · What it reads：Everything is **read-only**. The plugin never writes into another agent's data
directory, never touches a keychain or credential store, and makes no network
requests.

dsh-plugin-dew README · What it reads：| Agent | Sessions | Scheduled tasks | Source |
|---|:-:|:-:|---|
| Claude Code | ✅ | ⚠️ | `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl`, `~/.claude/scheduled-tasks/` |
| Codex | ✅ | ✅ | `~/.codex/sessions/`, `~/.codex/automations/` |
| Cursor | ✅ | — | `~/.cursor/projects/<slug>/agent-transcripts/` |
| DSH | ✅ | — | `$DSH_HOME` (default `~/.dsh`) and the DSH Desktop harness dir |

dsh-plugin-dew README · What it reads：⚠️ Claude Code scheduled tasks are implemented against the documented contract
but have never been observed on a real machine — the parser is defensive and
returns nothing rather than guessing.

dsh-plugin-dew README · How the states are decided：Each agent is different, and the honest summary is that **only some of this is
explicit**:

dsh-plugin-dew README · How the states are decided：- **Codex** and **DSH** write explicit lifecycle events (`task_started` /
  `task_complete`, `turn/start` / `turn/end`), so `running` and `done` are read,
  not inferred.
- **Claude Code** is inferred from the transcript tail: an `assistant` row with
  `stop_reason: "tool_use"` and no matching `tool_result` means a tool was
  requested and has not returned.
- **Cursor** has the least to work with — no `tool_result` rows and no
  timestamps — so its state rests on the last row plus the file's mtime.

dsh-plugin-dew README · How the states are decided：`needs_you` is **always** an inference. No agent writes a "waiting for approval"
event, so it is derived from a pending tool call that has gone quiet. The
threshold is per tool rather than a single number, because an approved long
`Bash` writes nothing to its log while it runs — silences of two to four minutes
are normal — and a flat threshold reports every slow command as a permission
prompt.

dsh-plugin-dew README · Privacy：`agent_sessions` returns a one-line summary of each session, which is an excerpt
of that conversation, and those summaries go to your model provider like any
other tool result. If that is not what you want:

```yaml
config:
  redactSummaries: true   # report states and projects, no conversation text
```

dsh-plugin-dew README · Configuration：```yaml
config:
  agents: []              # limit the scan, e.g. ["claude_code", "codex"]
  defaultWindowHours: 8   # lookback when a call does not specify one
  redactSummaries: false

dsh-plugin-dew README · Development：```bash
npm test        # node --test, no build step, no runtime dependencies
```

The plugin ships plain ESM — there is nothing to compile. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`
and `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` are peer dependencies supplied by any DSH profile.
